title: 1991 AHSME Problem 22
statement: Two circles are externally tangent. Lines \(PAB\) and \(PA'B'\) are common tangents with \(A\) and \(A'\) on the smaller circle and \(B\) and \(B'\) on the larger circle. If \(PA=AB=4,\) then the area of the smaller circle is

solutions.text:
Since \(PA=4\) and \(AB=4,\) we have \(PB=8.\) The homothety centered at \(P\) taking the smaller circle to the larger therefore has ratio \(2.\) If the smaller radius is \(r,\) its center is \(3r\) from \(P:\) the centers are on the same ray, their distances from \(P\) have ratio \(2,\) and their difference is \(r+2r=3r.\) Applying the right triangle formed by \(P,\) the small center, and \(A\), \[ PA^2=(3r)^2-r^2=8r^2. \] Thus \(16=8r^2,\) so \(r^2=2\) and the area is \(2\pi.\)

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: The two circles are related by a dilation centered at \(P\)
Use \(PA=4,\) \(PB=8\) to find the dilation ratio, then apply the tangent-length relation to the smaller circle
